leads.name: Groene beuk Bolwerken
leads.reason: evidence not conclusive enough this session
leads.note: Green (non-copper) beech, Statenbolwerk near nr 14, planted_band 1870-1880 but register's own history text speculates it could be from the park's original ~1832 planting, 'ongeveer 200 jaar oud' (roughly 200 years old). NOT the confirmed-dead tree (that is nr 1690404, a copper/red beech at nr 2 that blew down in storm Eunice, Feb 2022, see blocked list below), but the two are close in age, species-family and location, and I could not find an independent second source (photo, article, walking-guide mention) confirming this specific green beech is still standing post-2022. Worth a future pass with a street-level photo or the IVN/Bomenstichting guide's actual prose (register nr 1690403 was not found in a keyword search of that PDF's decoded text stream in this session, unlike nr 1696661/1696662/1696664/1686176 which were all found, which is itself mildly concerning and worth investigating directly). Addendum, 2026-08-22 deepen pass: a fresh WebSearch for 'Statenbolwerk Haarlem groene beuk boom monumentaal' surfaced only the already-known dead red beech (nr 1690404, poor-condition assessment from before it fell) and general Statenbolwerk monument listings; nothing new on this specific green beech's status. Still unresolved.

leads.name: Wintereik Ripperdapark
leads.reason: possible felling history at this exact park, could not confirm alive
leads.note: Register describes 'twee wintereiken' (two sessile oaks), planted_band 1900-1910, middle of the Ripperdapark lawn. A search turned up a 2016 gemeente Haarlem alderman letter titled 'kap eik Ripperdapark' (felling of an oak in Ripperdapark) and a monumentaltrees.com page for a 'Zachte eik' (downy oak, a different species name) in the same park with ground cracks and a severe lean noted as a stability concern. It is unclear whether that felling incident concerns this wintereik pair, the separately-named zachte eik, or a since-resolved case; monumentaltrees.com blocked WebFetch with a 403 (their server deliberately blocks automated fetches per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md, needs a real browser session to view). Left as a lead rather than delivered or blocked, because I have a specific death-adjacent signal but not enough to say alive or dead with confidence. Addendum, 2026-08-22 deepen pass: a fresh WebSearch for 'Ripperdapark Haarlem eik gekapt OR omgevallen wintereik 2022 OR 2023 OR 2024' found nothing about this park specifically (only an unrelated linden felled elsewhere in Haarlem in 2023). monumentaltrees.com remains 403-blocked to automated fetches; still needs a real browser session to check its Ripperdapark 'Zachte eik' page for the stability/lean details that could settle whether this is the same felling case. Still unresolved.

leads.name: Duplicate register entries already covered by haa_005 through haa_009
leads.note: Several Bolwerken-area register rows in this session's candidate list are the same physical trees as already-published haa_005 (Treurbeuk/Weeping Beech, Prinsenhof), haa_006 (Zomereik Wijngaardtuin), haa_007 (Moerascipressen Kenaupark), haa_008 (Platanengroep Kenaupark) and haa_009 (Hollandse linde Kenaupark): coordinates match within about 30m and species/common name match closely. No action needed, just recorded so a future pass does not re-research them.

leads.name: Zilveresdoorn Begraafplaats Kleverlaan
leads.reason: documented as nominated for felling; alive status genuinely uncertain
leads.note: Silver maple, 'Ten westen van Abri, Algemene begraafplaats Kleverlaan', planted band 1920-1930, in the same entrance cluster as haa_015/haa_016 delivered this session. A directly-fetched article (rodi.nl, 'Wandelen langs monumentale bomen in Hout, Bolwerken en Kleverlaan') states this tree 'stond tot Gerards verrassing niet in het landelijke register van monumentale bomen' (was not, to Gerard's surprise, in the national monumental-tree register at the time of writing) and is 'wegens diverse gebreken op de nominatie om gekapt te worden' (nominated for felling due to various defects). It is now IN the LRMB register (nr 1690405), so the register post-dates that article, but the felling nomination is not resolved either way by anything found this session: no news item or later source confirms whether it was actually felled or saved. Held back rather than delivered, because 'nominated for felling' is a real death-adjacent signal, not a normal missing-confirmation gap. A future pass with a recent photo, an aerial-imagery check (PDOK), or a local news search for the outcome could resolve this in minutes.

leads.name: Vleugelnootallee Kleverlaan
leads.reason: collectible-point question: an avenue of 20 trees, not a single point
leads.note: Register nr 1696670, 'Vleugelnootallee Kleverlaan' (Caucasian wingnut avenue), n_trees=20, planted band 1950-1960, place text 'Direct vanaf de ingang van het begraafpark loop je onder de vleugelnoten' (right from the cemetery entrance you walk beneath the wingnuts). A directly-fetched source (rodi.nl) independently describes this as an allee of 10 wingnut trees at the cemetery entrance (a discrepancy with the register's n_trees=20 worth noting, not resolved this session) and notes the trees were about 52 years old at the time of writing and therefore not yet old enough for the national register on their own steam. This reads as a genuine entrance corridor rather than a scattered inventory, which is the same test the Lomanstraat tunnel passed elsewhere on this site, but 20 (or even 10) trees along a walked-through avenue is a larger ensemble than any already-published Haarlem entry (the largest so far is a pair, haa_011/haa_018) and a run should not decide alone whether it is one collectible point or an excluded avenue. Left as a lead for a session to judge with eyes on a photo of the corridor, rather than delivered or blocked unilaterally.

leads.name: Zachte eik Frederikspark (voor Frederikspark 5A)
leads.reason: only a WebSearch AI summary found this session, not a directly-fetched source; treated as a lead per the search-summary rule
leads.note: Register nr 1691647, planted band 1850-1860, visitable=yes, visible=yes, n_trees=1, place text 'Frederikspark voor Frederikspark 5A'. A WebSearch summary (not independently verified on any page actually fetched this session) claimed a girth of 3.98 m for a 'Zachte eik' in Frederikspark, but per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md a search summary is a pointer, never a source, so that figure was deliberately not used. The register alone would be enough to deliver flagged with a single source, matching haa_016/haa_017/haa_020/haa_021 above; this one is left as a lead instead purely for time, not because the evidence is worse than those delivered ones. A future pass can simply deliver it the same way, or try to load the underlying page (haarlem.nl's tree-research page 403'd a plain fetch this session) for the girth figure directly.

blocked.name: Bruine beuk Bolwerken
blocked.reason: confirmed dead: blown down by storm Eunice, February 2022
blocked.note: This is a copper/red beech (Fagus sylvatica purpurea, 'rode beuk'/'bruine beuk' in Dutch) at Statenbolwerk near number 2. Two independent news sources confirm it blew down during storm Eunice (reported as 18 or 24 February 2022 depending on the source) at exactly this location: boomzorg.nl ('Haarlemse rode beuk (222) omgewaaid tijdens storm Eunice', giving the tree's age as 222 years, planted c.1800, at Staten Bolwerk designed by JD Zocher) and haarlem105.nl ('1800-2022: Eindelijk snijplanken van omgewaaide beuk in de Bolwerken'), which reports the fallen wood was later made into cutting boards (Haarlems Hout) and commemorative knives (Schreuder & Kraan), with an old nail from c.1830 found embedded in the trunk. The register's own planted_band for this entry (1860-1870) undershoots the true planting date the news coverage gives (c.1800/222 years old at time of falling), which is itself a useful reminder that a register's age band is a floor, not a fact, and should never be trusted over specific documented evidence. Never to be delivered as a live tree; recorded here so no future pass re-discovers and re-verifies the same dead tree from scratch.
